context.description: Ray is an AI compute engine. Ray consists of a core distributed runtime and a set of AI Libraries for accelerating ML workloads.

latestRelease.title: Ray-2.57.0
latestRelease.notes:
# Highlights

* **Ray Data:** In this Ray release, we've enabled `DataSourceV2` by default (#64821), so `read_parquet` and friends use the new scan/listing infrastructure with row-group-aware chunking and predicate splitting. Hash Shuffle V2 eliminates the aggregator actor pool. V1 had to provision that pool up front from an estimate of the input size, and its actors accumulated partition shards in actor heap memory, invisible to Ray and unspillable, until finalization. V2 replaces it with two stateless task-based operators, ShuffleMapOp --> ShuffleReduceOp, that pass shards through the object store, so intermediate state spills under pressure and no capacity has to be reserved in advance. The map/reduce barrier itself remains in both designs.
* HashShuffleV2 supports `join` ([#63598](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/63598), [#64538](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64538), [#64687](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64687)). This lets shuffles reuse standard map/reduce scheduling, backpressure, and resource accounting.
* **Ray Serve:** The HAProxy ingress is now distributed as the `ray-haproxy` PyPI package instead of being compiled into images, and it is the default HAProxy binary (#64141, #64163, #64164). We've also added gRPC support to the HAProxy direct-ingress path, including streaming, metrics, and custom request IDs (#63735, #64310, #64166, #64112). For Ray Serve LLM, we've added experimental KV-cache-aware request routing that tracks replica KV state through an event plane, tokenizes before routing, and routes on prefill/decode token load (#64084, #64085, #64097, #64224, #64327, #64400). KV cache-aware routing’s complete support will land in 2.58.
* **Ray Core:** We've added an embedded RocksDB storage backend for GCS fault tolerance (REP-64), selectable with `RAY_gcs_storage=rocksdb` and `RAY_gcs_storage_path` (#63657). GCS fault tolerance no longer requires an external Redis instance. We've also added a public API for topology-aware scheduling (#63479, #63740).

# Ray Data

### 🎉 New Features
* Enable `DataSourceV2` by default via `DataContext.use_datasource_v2` (#64821)
* New task-based hash shuffle v2 (`ShuffleMapOp` → `ShuffleReduceOp`) with `join`, multi-input reduce, downstream map fusion, and reducer remote args, behind an env flag (#63598, #64538, #64687, #64438, #64302, #64532, #64481)
* Add a `Catalog` abstraction with a `UnityCatalog` implementation that can be passed to `read_*`, and Unity Catalog write support for Parquet and Iceberg (#64193, #64519)
* Add `read_zarr` for Zarr datasets (#63003) and `read_lerobot` for LeRobot v3 datasets (#63821)
* Add `PushdownCountFiles` optimization to answer `count()` from Parquet footers (#64763)
* Add common subexpression elimination to the expression optimizer (#63974)
* Add GPU support for `Aggregate` (#63708)
* Make dataset iteration metrics queryable per split (#64608)
* Add custom operator stats to capture worker-side metrics during task execution (#64221)
* Refactor usage collection into an extensible `UsageCallback` (#64500)
* Export `from_blocks` from `ray.data` (#64127)
* Add support for `rapidsmpf-26.4.0` (#64324)

### 💫 Enhancements
* Hide Ray Data internal frames from user-code error tracebacks (#64587)
* Run projection/predicate pushdown before limit pushdown, block optimization of non-deterministic expressions, and make fuse checks consistent between the logical and physical optimizers (#64651, #64165, #63936)
* Add a two-mode block metadata fetch behind a single `MetadataFetcher` interface (#64378)
* Use work stealing for file listing and a dynamic work queue for traversals (#64675, #64388)
* Speed up `ExecutionResources` and the reservation/budget loops on the scheduling hot path (#63964)
* Fix `O(n^2)` schema reconciliation in `unify_schemas` and avoid per-column `Series` materialization in tensor-column casting (#64555, #64038)
* Decouple collate and memory pinning in `iter_torch_batches`, add per-stage training-thread blocking attribution, bound in-flight `iter_threaded` items, and finalize after reordering under `preserve_order` (#64653, #64183, #64219, #64282)
* Add default logical memory for map operators, wire the materializing-op filter into `OpResourceAllocator` budgeting, and move `estimate_object_store_usage` into the physical op (#63814, #63665, #63961)
* Decrease the downstream backpressure ratio to 2.0 (#64352)
* Route native `S3FileSystem` downloads to the PyArrow threaded path (#64089)
* Size hash-shuffle aggregators via bounded online sampling and add a timeout to the batched `ray.get` when fetching partitions (#63929, #64256)
* Replace manual block reference accounting with Ray Core out-of-scope object callbacks (#64011, #64157, #64191)
* Default `read_numpy` to `allow_pickle=False` and make it manually configurable (#64684)
* Make `write_lance(mode=CREATE)` error instead of silently overwriting (#64364)
* Expand `DistributionTracker` with `merge()` and p25/p75, and add dead node counts and detected issues to usage collection (#64074, #64459, #64198)
* Remove cluster autoscaler v1, rename the subcluster label key to `ray-subcluster`, avoid scaling nodegroups dedicated to the head node, and quiet autoscaling coordinator logs (#64380, #64003, #63918, #63534)
* Delay the "cluster resources not enough" warning until an operator is persistently starved, and lower the high-memory warning threshold (#63969, #64124)
* Remove `ExecutionPlan`, `_num_outputs`, `batch_format` on `AllToAllOperators`, and `InheritBatchFormatRule`; use `input_dependencies` in logical operators (#63662, #64167, #64152, #64149, #64148)
* Deprecate low-level scheduling APIs (`DataContext.scheduling_strategy`, `actor_locality_enabled`, `exclude_resources`, `local://`) ahead of the actor-only rearchitecture (#64632)
* Migrate the Daft dependency from `getdaft` to `daft` (#64240)
* Migrate `apply_chat_template`/`tokenize`/`detokenize` callers to `*_stage` form, and remove `PrepareImageStage` while deprecating the `image` row column (#63590, #63570)

### 🔨 Fixes
* Fix `TensorDtype.__from_arrow__` crash on empty tensor columns (#64767)
* Fix Arrow-backed `to_pandas` regressions with an opt-out flag and int/float block overflow handling (#64768)
* Fix read-only hash array crash in hash partition (#64552, #64559)
* Fix streaming-generator hang on a plasma-resident return object (#64386)
* Fix Parquet write overflow for string/binary columns larger than 2 GiB (#64212)
* Fix Parquet sampling hang on a permanent `OSError` (#64342)
* Fix the BigQuery datasink to handle empty blocks (#60797)
* Make `PandasBlock.size_bytes` deterministic (#64393)
* Propagate branch in `_append_and_commit()` for the Iceberg overwrite save mode (#63922)
* Propagate `isolate_read_workers` to `DatasourceV2` (#65191, #65207)
* Fix cross-region S3 bucket access in the obstore download path (#63890)
* Restore `safe_round` in the `ExecutionResources` hot path (#64296)
* Log both the wrapped and wrapper exception in `iterate_with_retry` (#64639)
* Add `tf-keras` to the `text_embedding` pip packages (#64889, #64968)
* Fix `build_processor` failing with vLLM >= 0.19, correct its `config` type hint, and add `request_timeout_s` to `ServeDeploymentProcessor` to prevent indefinite hangs (#64337, #64098, #64496)
* Fix type hints in `throughput_solver.py` (#64289)

### 📖 Documentation
* Add a guide on avoiding out-of-memory errors and improve the existing OOM docs (#64046, #64297)
* Document the best practice for isolating Ray Data workers from training nodes (#64588)
* Document running two datasets in one cluster (#64200)
* Move the `read_zarr` guide back into its docstring (#64409)
* Remove Ray Data and DAG docstring ignores from pydoclint (#63634)

# Ray Serve

### 🎉 New Features
* Distribute HAProxy through the `ray-haproxy` PyPI package, make it the default binary, and remove the from-source build (#64141, #64163, #64164)
* Add gRPC support to the HAProxy direct ingress, including streaming, unary-unary metrics, and custom request IDs (#63735, #64310, #64166, #64112)
* Emit request and system metrics from HAProxy (#64329, #64255)
* Support `root_path` in the HAProxy ingress (#64295)
* Add a per-replica metadata hook exposed on `ReplicaSelection` (#63948)

### 💫 Enhancements
* HAProxy stability: graceful drain waits for in-flight and queued requests, replicas quiesce before reporting shutdown complete, dispatches cancelled by replica gRPC stop are retried, reload takeover is verified by pid, and `close-spread-time` is set in the template (#63886, #63920, #63995, #64022, #64063, #63996)
* Make direct-ingress port reconcile incremental and skip it entirely when ingress membership is unchanged (#64508, #64676)
* Controller performance: `O(1)` version-filtered replica counts, in-place health-check reconcile in the deployment-state loop, and a fast-path orphaned-actor check (#64699, #64507, #64511)
* Freeze GC after replica initialization by default (#64742)
* Eager-load proxy imports (#64113)
* Pin the replica actor to bundle 0 of its placement group and track actor `fallback_strategy` on `DeploymentSchedulingInfo` (#62693, #64346)
* Deprecate `HTTPOptions.location` in favor of `proxy_location`, raise on non-zero `HTTPOptions.num_cpus`, and warn on other deprecated HTTP options (#64479, #64418, #63604)
* Raise a clear error when a custom request router or `serve.multiplexed` is used on an ingress deployment under direct ingress (#64211, #64045)
* Recover ingress request router pin-misses via the fallback proxy instead of returning 503 (#64218)
* Add `RAY_SERVE_CONTROLLER_METRICS_INCLUDE_HIGH_CARDINALITY_TAGS` to control controller metric tags (#63642)
* Default `RAY_SERVE_PORT_QUARANTINE_S` to hard-stop-after plus a margin (#64021)
* Defer the "application ready" log until proxies are ready (#64010)
* Dedup ingress replica and proxy metrics code, and migrate `parse_uri` from `_private` to `_common` (#64041, #64371)
* Enforce `mypy` and `pyrefly` type checking on clean Serve files (#64662)
* Fail loudly when subclassing `@serve.ingress` with a sync `__init__` (#63413)
* Supply a safe default request id header value in direct ingress (#64118)

### 🔨 Fixes
* Fix `serve.ingress(FastAPI())` pickling and `include_router` under FastAPI >= 0.137 (#64814, #64531)
* Fix an idle worker leak that caused OOM on the Ray head node (#63597)
* Fix `serve.shutdown()` skipping live shutdown when the cached controller client is stale after a driver reconnect (#64660)
* Preserve the deployment actor class across a config re-apply (#64411)
* Fix rank corruption on controller recovery after a lightweight reconfigure (#64636)
* Fix `route=None` crash in direct-ingress metrics reporting (#64645)
* Fix the direct-ingress backpressure counter leak on cancel-while-queued and clean up the leaked receive task on request timeout (#64348, #64123)
* Fix HAProxy `healthz` falling through to 404 when there are no backends (#64582)
* Guard request router backoff against `OverflowError` (#64539)
* Fix a slot leak race in `SingletonThreadRouter.choose_replica` (#63649)
* Fix a type regression in `RAY_SERVE_HAPROXY_CLOSE_SPREAD_TIME_S` (#64752)
* Fix Serve tests broken by protobuf 7 (#64362)

### 📖 Documentation
* Fix the `RequestRouterConfig` stats docstring to reference `record_routing_stats` (#64086)

# Ray Train

### 🎉 New Features
* Add preemption handling: a preemption watcher for node-drain observability, with the signal fanned out to workers (#63807, #64099)

### 💫 Enhancements
* Make Train v1 and v2 use the autoscaling coordinator (#64824, #64936)
* Restrict `ray.train.report(checkpoint)` to in-band checkpoints only (#63645)
* Make `Result.from_path` read-only (#64340)
* Add compute-time metrics to `tune_torch_benchmark.py` (#64274)
* Update TensorFlow/Keras examples and tests for Keras 3 compatibility (#64276)

### 🔨 Fixes
* Fix `CometLoggerCallback` mutating the caller's result dict via `result.pop()` (#64570)
* Fix the `WorkerMetricsCallback` method name to match the `WorkerCallback` interface (#64568)

### 📖 Documentation
* Document the unsafe deserialization risk in `TorchCheckpoint.get_model()` and `FrameworkCheckpoint.get_preprocessor()` (#64586)
* Fix docstring style and enable `--check-style-mismatch=True` in pydoclint (#63988)
* Enumerate the accepted resource keys for `ScalingConfig` (#63449)

# Ray Tune

### 💫 Enhancements
* Make `BayesOptSearch` float-hash precision configurable (#63914)
* Require `optuna>=3.0.0` in `OptunaSearch` (#64242)

### 🔨 Fixes
* Respect `max_concurrent_trials` for custom searchers (#63770)

### 📖 Documentation
* Warn when `BayesOptSearch` stops early on convergence, and document `patience`/`skip_duplicate` (#64288)
* Restructure the Tune example pages and add PyTorch Lightning examples to the examples README (#63460, #63438)
* Document nested-metric keys in `ResultGrid.get_best_result` and add a conditional search-space example to `tune.sample_from` (#63445, #63443)

# Ray LLM

### 🎉 New Features
* Add KV-cache-aware request routing: `KVAwareRouter`/`KVRouterActor` interfaces, replica tracking, an event plane, pre-routing tokenization, token-level request lifecycle tracking, and prefill/decode token-load-aware routing (#64084, #64085, #64097, #64224, #64327, #64400)
* Switch the Ray Serve SGLang engine to the sglang `RayEngine`, reach control-plane parity, and support Ray Serve direct streaming by serving SGLang's native OpenAI app (#62888, #63021, #64611)
* Add the MoRIIO KV-connector backend for prefill/decode disaggregation, with cross-node worker IP advertisement via a vLLM plugin (#63951, #64067)
* Enable the `/classify` and `/pooling` endpoints in direct-streaming mode (#64494)
* Add a Ray Serve LLM SGLang metrics dashboard (#64797, #65083)

### 💫 Enhancements
* Upgrade vLLM to 0.25.1 (#64082, #64483, #64697)
* Delegate prefill/decode orchestration to the KV-connector backend and avoid double prompt tokenization in disaggregation (#63950, #64049)
* Make `request.request_id` authoritative for the engine and stop clobbering an explicitly set request id with the Serve id (#63949, #64044)
* Parse the direct-streaming routing payload for body-aware routers, and add direct streaming session-affinity tests (#64328, #63927, #64266)
* Use `asyncio.create_task` instead of `ensure_future` in `KVRouterActor` (#64546)
* Add a cluster filter to the Serve LLM Grafana dashboard (#64596)
* Validate `accelerator_type` for CPU vLLM engine configs (#64235)
* Use `model_id` rather than the remote URI as the cache identifier in `VLLMEngineConfig` (#64110)
* Remove the Serve LLM config generator (#64075)

### 🔨 Fixes
* Fix malformed PromQL in the Serve LLM Grafana dashboard (#63893)

### 📖 Documentation
* Add a custom vLLM model guide and update the vLLM embedding model example (#64594, #64504)
* Improve the Serve LLM docs landing pages, add a config reference, and document direct streaming and the ingress request router (#64076, #63860)
* Fix 404s in the Serve LLM examples sidebar links (#64209)

# Ray RLlib

### 🎉 New Features
* Add a pull-based `EnvRunnerStateServer` for async weight sync (#63849)
* Expose the count of `EnvRunner`s dropped on `timeout_seconds` calls (#63493)

### 💫 Enhancements
* Upgrade the example vision stack to MobileNet v3 and remove MobileNet v2 torchhub usage (#64031, #64028)

### 🔨 Fixes
* Narrow `from_checkpoint` expectations to avoid silent failures (#63614)
* Require `MultiRLModuleSpec.rl_module_specs` to be a dict (#64785)
* Fix the perpetual pending state in offline evaluation during Tune (#64453)
* Fix RLlib with Tune by reverting the `AlgorithmConfig.to_dict()` change for the new API stack (#63695, #64501)
* Fix ONNX export under torch 2.9 by bumping `onnxscript` and migrating to the dynamo exporter (#64410, #64033)
* Apply observation filters in `compute_single_action()` on the old API stack (#64088)

### 📖 Documentation
* Revamp the RL modules docs and speed up the docs tests (#64505)
* Fix the outdated parametric-action-spaces link in `rllib-algorithms` (#63435)

# Ray Core

### 🎉 New Features
* Add an embedded RocksDB storage backend for GCS fault tolerance (REP-64), selected via `RAY_gcs_storage=rocksdb` and `RAY_gcs_storage_path` (#63657)
* Add a public API for topology-aware scheduling via `topology_strategy` (#63479, #63740)
* Implement backpressure for async streaming generators, add actor-level backpressure config, and add `_num_objects_per_yield` (#64383, #63310, #63943)
* Implement `RayTaskEventRecorder` as the first step of moving task events out of GCS (#64168)
* Drain the node on `SIGTERM` before shutting down `ray start --block` (#64454)
* Add `tpu.dispatch` syntax sugar and a JAX profiler for TPU (#64493, #62371)
* Publicize `__ray_call__` as a `DeveloperAPI` for running closures on actors (#64367)
* Add the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 accelerator type and update the AMD accelerator manager (#64428, #62477)
* RDT: enable the `LIBFABRIC` backend for NIXL and upgrade NIXL to v1.2.0 (#62339, #63980)
* Add an owner-driven `FreeLocalObjects` RPC and remove the original `FreeObjects` RPC and `ObjectEviction` pubsub (#63218, #63181)

### 💫 Enhancements
* Actor scalability: prefill the placement-group bundle cache at creation to remove an actor submission bottleneck, and construct gRPC metric objects once per process instead of per request (#64649, #64732)
* Bound the GCS worker table by evicting old dead-worker entries, prioritized by exit type (#64612, #64729)
* Batch object-manager `Pull` RPCs by destination node and read spilled object chunks in bulk instead of byte-by-byte (#64225, #63830)
* Post all object pubsub publishes to the IO thread to relieve lock contention (#63983)
* Autoscaler: improve v2 scheduler performance for large clusters, handle deleted node types in the metrics reporter, and support env-var configuration for log rotation (#64175, #64184, #63955)
* Integrate `IOContextMonitor` into GCS, update its metrics, and exclude `ray_syncer_io_context` and `task_io_context` from health checks while raising the probe deadline to 30s (#63930, #63975, #64522, #64421)
* Continue the `ClockInterface` migration in the core worker and dependency-inject `PeriodicalRunnerInterface` (#63956, #63994, #64061, #64029)
* Enable `process_group_cleanup_enabled` by default and fix graceful-shutdown cleanup (#64407)
* Make owned object metrics lazy, compute per-component memory usage in MiB, scope `prom_metrics_service_discovery.json` to the session dir, and set the OpenTelemetry resource identity (#64093, #63932, #63850, #63921)
* Re-emit per-state task, actor, and placement group gauges every metrics tick and retain gauge observations for a TTL, so live series survive a missed scrape (#64524, #64633)
* Add the GPU UUID to the labels of GPU metrics (#65113, #65134)
* Log a hint to the driver when system overhead exceeds reserved system memory (#64270)
* Validate explicit zero resource isolation overrides and move memory monitors into `common/monitor` (#63864, #64491)
* Prioritize tasks over actors when killing under memory pressure (#64170)
* Bail on `AdjustWorkerOomScore` read failure and clamp the score to `[-1000, 1000]` (#62713)
* Cap the `runtime_env` `parse_uri` package name length to avoid `ENAMETOOLONG` (#64339)
* Scope the raylet's forced GC to backstop actor handle cycle deadlocks (#63939)
* Support joining fibers before exiting the fiber runner thread (#64405)
* Internal cleanups: remove callbacks from `TaskToExecute`, split task/resource preparation utils out of `_raylet.pyx`, consolidate the GCS dedicated `io_context` policy, and rename `OnDemandBroadcasting` (#64182, #63088, #63931, #63855)

### 🔨 Fixes
* Fix a Python 3.14 async-actor memory leak by re-anchoring the stack (#65177)
* Fix a deadlock between metric registration and `collect()` in `OpenTelemetryMetricRecorder` (#64946, #65094)
* Fix multi-threaded actor graceful shutdown (#64019)
* Streaming generator fixes: remove ref stream callbacks that caused a reconstruction hang, fail fast on a replay object-count mismatch, remove the implicit `__dealloc__()`, and honor `timeout_s` in the end-of-stream `ray.get` (#64581, #64394, #64333, #64014)
* Fix pipelining of actor argument fetches while an actor task is running (#63079)
* Fix a dangling reference in `GetSchedulingClassDescriptor` (#64707)
* Fix a pgid cleanup leak in the job supervisor (#64746)
* Fix the raylet drain path reading stale object store memory usage (#64415)
* Avoid a GCS crash on Redis connection loss in `RedisResponseFn` (#64204)
* Fix the actor `working_dir` being overridden by the job-level `py_driver_sys_path` (#63756)
* Fix `RAY_CHECK` failures caused by double `ray.cancel()` and keyboard interrupts (#63663)
* Fix `event_logger` and `export_event_logger` to flush all handlers safely (#63947)
* Default `TaskProfileEvent.extra_data_` to `{}` to avoid a JSON decoding error in the State API, and normalize the `cmdline` field in the `StatsPayload` schema (#64589, #64286)
* Autoscaler v2: fix `ALLOCATION_TIMEOUT` worker replacement ordering and the `RAY_STOP_REQUESTED` → `RAY_RUNNING` fallback when drain has succeeded (#63815, #63424)
* Jobs: replace an `assert` with `RuntimeError` in `put_status` and avoid mutating `runtime_env` during submission (#64569, #63990)
* Improve the error message when `RAY_ADDRESS` is set to an HTTP address (#64180)
* Define `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` globally for Windows builds (#64361)
* Wait for subprocesses to terminate in `ray.shutdown()` (#63655)
* Fix the per-process GPU memory utilization dashboard stat (#61412)

### 📖 Documentation
* Update the OOM documentation to use resource isolation mode (#63652)
* Clarify the KubeRay autoscaler `restartPolicy` requirement (#64855)
* Document the `name` parameter for `task.options()` (#63450)
* Enforce Doxygen documentation style for coding agents and remove Ray Core docstring ignores from pydoclint (#64188, #63639)

# Dashboard

### 🎉 New Features
* Implement the frontend UI for Platform Events (#63332)

### 💫 Enhancements
* Link workers to actor detail pages and handle nil IDs (#63795)
* Support a Grafana Cloud metrics fallback (#64138)
* Format `RuntimeEnvState.creation_time_ms` as a duration (#64207)
* Diagnose dashboard-agent event-loop stalls (#64436)
* Log errors when job submission fails in `JobHead` and stop configuring the root logger on module import (#64443, #64463)

### 🔨 Fixes
* Fix local file inclusion in the `/logs` API endpoint by rejecting absolute paths and `..` components in `LogAgentV1Grpc.ListLogs()` (#64701)
* Fix TPU metrics (#63998)
* Fix task grouping by custom task name in the Dashboard API (#63820)
* Fix an "automaticaly" typo in the Grafana dashboard descriptions (#64614)

# Ray Wheels and Images

* Build and publish Python 3.14 wheels and images, add py3.14 TPU base deps, refresh the py3.14 locks, and add a py3.14 smoke release test (#64754, #64750, #64857, #64938).
* Build and publish `cu130` variants for the `ray` and `ray-extra` images (#63972, #63801).
* Add a py3.13 `ray-ml` image with `torchft-nightly` (#63587).
* Add `ray-haproxy` to the `ray[serve]` extra and base requirements, and bump it to 2.8.25 for CVE-2026-55203/55204 (#64141, #64430).
* Unify `requirements_compiled` across Python versions and upgrade the HuggingFace stack to `datasets` 4.x (#64257, #64054).
* Fix the vendored RocksDB build: use Make instead of Ninja to repair aarch64 core builds, drop `-Wl,-pie` from the TSAN link flags, and silence TSAN false-positive races (#64748, #64917, #64937, #64759).

# Documentation

* Added `AGENTS.md` with the AI-assisted contribution policy, routed `.claude/CLAUDE.md` to it, and added a documentation style and grammar guide (#64419, #64518).
* Converted the ray-contribute developer guides from RST to MyST, soft-wrapped prose across `doc/source`, and added an rst-to-myst conversion skill (#64100, #64111, #64115, #64136, #64259, #64279, #64135).
* Added a unified APIs navigation section, generated API stubs without a full doc build, and greened the API-doc consistency check with reverse/dedup policies and a split whitelist (#64387, #64423, #64420, #64783, #64786, #64808, #64818).
* Added curated page descriptions for nav pages (SEO and `llms.txt`) and a custom 404 page with absolute URLs (#64330, #64603).
* Built Read the Docs incrementally from the doc build cache, repaired cache production, and skipped RtD PR builds for code-only PRs (#64277, #64414, #64482, #64599, #64547, #64480).
* Hardened doc template fetches: pinned to specific build ids, guarded zip extraction against path traversal, failed the build loudly on fetch failure, and removed outdated templates now synced at build time (#64637, #64669, #64629, #64635, #63971).
* Upgraded Sphinx to 8.2.3 on Python 3.11, decoupled Sphinx from the test/CI dependency stack, and fixed moved intersphinx inventory URLs (#64070, #63962, #64516).
* KubeRay: added an IPPR user guide, documented RayCronJob timezone support and autoscaler command overwrite, updated the RayJob agent sandbox docs, and refreshed the Serve High Throughput guide for Ray 2.56 (#63212, #64444, #63627, #64460, #64144).
* Added notebook tests for the lightweight Ray Core examples and recorded the Train example notebooks that are intentionally untested (#64313, #64318).
* Refreshed the ecosystem page, added a Ray + Agent Sandbox example, and renamed the AI chat widget to "Ray Docs" (#64156, #64047, #64351).

highlights: Ray Data: In this Ray release, we've enabled DataSourceV2 by default (#64821), so readparquet and friends use the new scan/listing infrastructure with row-group-aware chunking and predicate splitting. Hash Shuffle V2 eliminates the aggregat
HashShuffleV2 supports join (#63598, #64538, #64687). This lets shuffles reuse standard map/reduce scheduling, backpressure, and resource accounting.

Ray Serve: The HAProxy ingress is now distributed as the ray-haproxy PyPI package instead of being compiled into images, and it is the default HAProxy binary (#64141, #64163, #64164). We've also added gRPC support to the HAProxy direct-ingr

Ray Core: We've added an embedded RocksDB storage backend for GCS fault tolerance (REP-64), selectable with RAYgcsstorage=rocksdb and RAYgcsstoragepath (#63657). GCS fault tolerance no longer requires an external Redis instance. We've also
Enable DataSourceV2 by default via DataContext.usedatasourcev2 (#64821)

signals.title: [Core][Feature request] Promote `actor_handle._actor_id` to public API
signals.text: We should promote `_actor_id` to public API and also make it a usable string, e.g. `repr` does not add anything except the ID. ``` >>> a._actor_id ActorID(811a6143d62d08e4d6e447c21c000000) # This should change to just return '811a6143d62d08e4d6e447c21c000000' ``` Example use case is in combination with the State API: ``` import ray ray.init() @ray.remote class A: pass a = A.remote() # Use here instead of this hack obj_ref = str(a).replace('Actor(A, ', '').replace(')', '') from ray.experimental.state.api import get_actor print(get_actor(id=obj_ref)) ```

signals.title: [Core] Actor RSS does not drop even if all object refs are released
signals.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen I created an actor with a function `get`. Each `get` constructs a torch tensor. Driver calls its `get` function for 3000 times and get the results. After clearing all the object refs, the actor rss memory should drop but it didn't. #### memray graph ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f654e39-b158-4f53-b589-13cfac85b190) #### pmap check After seeing "done!" (i.e. all the object refs should be released), I `pmap -x <pid>` the actor process and found plasma mmap shared memory occupies about 2.6g rss memory. I guess the objects are not released (or fd are not unmapped). #### raylet log Another discovery is the raylet debug log. I checked the logic of `MarkObjectAsUnused`, which tells the client to munmap the object only when ref count = 0. However, all objects in raylet log shows `should_unmap = 0`. Since no more logs about real ref count in `MarkObjectAsUnused`, I can hardly tell if it works as expected. ``` [2025-05-23 14:51:57,409 D 1580641 1580721] (raylet) store.cc:258: Object 00ef45ccd0112571ffffffffffffffffffffffff0100000004e1f505 no longer in use by client, should_unmap = 0 ``` Related code: ```c++ // ray-master\src\ray\object_manager\plasma\connection.h bool MarkObjectAsUnused(const ray::ObjectID &object_id) override { // ... size_t &ref_cnt = ref_cnt_iter->second; RAY_CHECK_GT(ref_cnt, static_cast<size_t>(0)); ref_cnt -= 1; if (ref_cnt == 0) { fallback_allocated_fds_ref_count_.erase(ref_cnt_iter); used_fds_.erase(fd); // Next SendFd call will send this fd again. return true; } ``` ```c++ // ray-master\src\ray\object_manager\plasma\store.cc bool PlasmaStore::RemoveFromClientObjectIds(const ObjectID &object_id, const std::shared_ptr<Client> &client) { auto &object_ids = client->GetObjectIDs(); auto it = object_ids.find(object_id); if (it != object_ids.end()) { bool should_unmap = client->MarkObjectAsUnused(object_id); RAY_LOG(DEBUG) << "Object " << object_id << " no longer in use by client, should_unmap = " << should_unmap; // Decrease reference count. object_lifecycle_mgr_.RemoveReference(object_id); ``` #### core worker log From the perspective of core-worker, no munmap log ("ClientMmapTableEntry dtor munmaped ") is observed. Related code: ```c++ ClientMmapTableEntry::~ClientMmapTableEntry() { #ifdef _WIN32 r = UnmapViewOfFile(pointer_) ? 0 : -1; #else r = munmap(pointer_, length_); #endif if (r != 0) { RAY_LOG(ERROR) << "munmap returned " << r << ", errno = " << errno; } else { RAY_LOG(DEBUG) << "ClientMmapTableEntry dtor munmaped " << fd_.first << ", " << fd_.second << ", addr " << pointer_ << ", size " << length_; } } ``` ### Versions / Dependencies linux x86-64 ray 2.44.1 pytorch 2.6.0 memray 1.17.1 ### Reproduction script ```python import ray import memray import time import os import torch os.environ["RAY_BACKEND_LOG_LEVEL"] = "debug" ray.init() @ray.remote class TD: def __init__(self): memray.Tracker("memray_output.bin").__enter__() def get(self): tensor = torch.randn(262144, dtype=torch.float32) return tensor td_actor = TD.remote() def driver(): results = [] for _ in range(3000): result = td_actor.get.remote() results.append(result) ray.get(results) results.clear() driver() print('done!') time.sleep(60) ray.shutdown() ``` After seeing "done!", try `pmap -x <actor_pid>`. To see memray graphs, type `memray flamegraph memray_output.bin` after the program completes. ### Issue Severity Medium: It is a significant difficulty but I can work around it.

signals.title: [RLlib] Checkpointing fails with CUDA GPU learner using the new API stack
signals.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen I'm running PPO learner on CUDA GPU with `tune.fit()` and `checkpoint_config=tune.CheckpointConfig(checkpoint_at_end=True)` Example learners setup: ``` .learners( num_learners=1, num_gpus_per_learner=1 ) ``` ### Expected behavior Checkpoint is saved ### Actual behavior Checkpoint save fails with exception: ``` RuntimeError: Attempting to deserialize object on a CUDA device but torch.cuda.is_available() is False. If you are running on a CPU-only machine, please use torch.load with map_location=torch.device('cpu') to map your storages to the CPU. ``` ### Further information Given that I have torch available and I can see with nvidia-smi/nvtop that the learning really runs on my GPU, it seems like the checkpointing is done on some node that, for some reason, does not have access to torch. The checkpoint save does succeed after GPU learning under these conditions: * If I run the training without tune in a simple loop that builds the algorithm, calls algorithm.train() and saves the checkpoint with algorithm.save_to_path() * If I run similar setup with tune using the old api stack, i.e. with ``` .api_stack( enable_rl_module_and_learner=False, enable_env_runner_and_connector_v2=False, ) ``` * If I run the original case with `num_learners=0`, which according to the documentation means it is running a local learner, the checkpoint save succeeds. signals.title: [Rllib] new API stack uses >2X VRAM of old stack
signals.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen A major limiter in our team moving to the new API stack is currently the much higher VRAM memory use, when using the new stack we are unable to use the same model/batch sizes we are using on the old stack. We are using an RNN style model using PPO RLLIB config ```yml # stack switch enable_env_runner_and_connector_v2: False enable_rl_module_and_learner: False # new api stack train_batch_size_per_learner: 12000 num_gpus_per_learner: 1 # old api stack train_batch_size: 12000 num_gpus: 1 # generic minibatch_size: 1200 horizon: 1200 rollout_fragment_length: 600 num_env_runners: 20 num_cpus_per_env_runner: 1 num_cpus_per_main_process: 1 batch_mode: complete_episodes count_steps_by: "agent_steps" entropy_coeff: .001 clip_param: .2 grad_clip: 2.5 lambda: .95 gamma: .999 placement_strategy: SPREAD ``` ``` os.environ["PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF"] = "expandable_segments:True" torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32" torch.backends.cudnn.fp32_precision = "tf32" ``` are set in our module file OLD API STACK steady state vram usage on my local laptop: ``` +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | NVIDIA-SMI 535.274.02 Driver Version: 535.274.02 CUDA Version: 12.2 | |-----------------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+ | GPU Name Persistence-M | Bus-Id Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. See documentation for Memory Management (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda.html#environment-variables) ``` ### Versions / Dependencies ray 2.51.1 python 3.11 torch 2.10 ### Reproduction script provided rllib configuration above to repo, any environment should work ### Issue Severity High: It blocks me from completing my task.
signals.author: Phirefly9

signals.title: Supporting Host Name routing rather than primarily relying on IP address/port
signals.text: ### Description Add a RAY_NODE_USE_HOSTNAME environment variable. When set to 1, Ray uses socket.gethostname() instead of an IP address for node identification. The node address is a string throughout the entire path (get_node_ip_address() → GCS registration → NodeInfo.node_manager_address → gRPC connections), so substituting a hostname at the entry point appears to propagate cleanly. In fact, we've POCd this with a Ray fork and it is working well. ### Use case Ray identifies nodes by IP address, and this convention propagates through to gRPC TLS handshakes, where certificate SANs are validated against the connection address. However, many organizational Certificate Authorities — including mine — issue certificates with hostname SANs only, not IP SANs. As a result, operators are forced to either stand up a separate private CA dedicated to Ray or disable TLS verification entirely — neither of which is great. I'd be happy to contribute this change upstream if the approach aligns with the project's direction. Additionally, I'd love to understand why Ray chose IP-based identification in the first place. There may be assumptions elsewhere in the system that I'm not seeing. Are there known cases where hostname resolution would break things? Thanks!
signals.author: shayansadeghieh

signals.title: [Data] AutoscalingCoordinator._reallocate_resources is O(R·N²) and holds its lock, starving concurrent datasets at scale (op_budget→0)
signals.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen On a large autoscaling cluster (~840 nodes) running several concurrent Ray Data datasets with the V2 cluster autoscaler (RAY_DATA_CLUSTER_AUTOSCALER=V2, the default), datasets get op_budget=0 and stall — every map op shows Tasks: N [backpressured:tasks(ResourceBudget)], throughput collapses — while the cluster has resources. Driver logs repeat: ``` WARNING default_autoscaling_coordinator.py:134 -- Failed to get allocated resources for data-dataset_XXX_0. (consecutive failures: N) Returning cached value. ray.exceptions.GetTimeoutError: Get timed out: some object(s) not ready. ``` ### Root cause (py-spy confirmed, Ray 2.54.1) The cluster-singleton AutoscalingCoordinator actor is single-threaded, and _reallocate_resources runs an O(R·N²) triple loop while holding the only self._lock, blocking client get_allocated_resources/request_resources until they time out. Two compounding facts: 1. The request is one bundle per cluster node. DefaultClusterAutoscalerV2.try_trigger_scaling builds active_bundles from _get_node_resource_spec_and_count() (= ray.nodes(), one bundle per alive node). cap_resource_request_to_limits() always includes all active bundles and only caps the pending/scale-up bundles to resource_limits. So the request length B ≈ N (node count), independent of the dataset's concurrency or resource_limits. 2. _reallocate_resources is for R requesters: for B≈N bundles: for N nodes: _maybe_subtract_resources (+ a full copy.deepcopy of all node resources, recomputed from scratch). Under over-subscription the inner node loop rarely breaks early (nodes exhausted) → ~R·N² iterations. Measured (pure Python, R=7): single _reallocate_resources ≈ 1.8s at N=836 (B=150→0.21s, 600→1.27s, 836→1.82s; linear in B≈N). It's invoked on every request_resources (the request changes each cycle since it's rebuilt from live ray.nodes()), every cancel_request, and every 20s tick — no coalescing. With ~7 datasets refreshing ~every 10s, reallocations run back-to-back (≈0.7/s × 1.8s ⇒ a single core saturated). py-spy record (20s) shows 96% of coordinator CPU in _reallocate_resources/_maybe_subtract_resources (the autoscaler SDK call is ~3%). A concurrent get_allocated_resources sits blocked on self._lock, hits GetTimeoutError, and the client falls back to a cached/empty allocation → ResourceManager.global_limits = min(resource_limits, 0) = 0 → op_budget 0 → backpressure. This scales with cluster size N, not job count: because B≈N and the loop is N², even 2–3 concurrent datasets can saturate the coordinator on a large cluster. resource_limits does not mitigate it (the cap doesn't shrink the per-node active bundles). ### Versions / Dependencies Ray 2.54.1; RAY_DATA_CLUSTER_AUTOSCALER=V2 (default). ### Reproduction script - At scale: ≥7 concurrent datasets over-subscribing a ~840-node cluster → all hit GetTimeoutError + op_budget=0. - Offline (no cluster): _AutoscalingCoordinatorActor deps are injectable — construct with get_cluster_nodes returning N≈836 fake nodes, register R requesters (request_remaining=True), and time _reallocate_resources() → ~1.8s at N=836, R=7. (Standalone script available.) ### Issue Severity None
signals.author: qyzhaoxun

signals.title: RDT: Enable ray.put from a non ray actor
signals.text: ### Description rdt: enable ray.put() and free() from driver process with a one-sided transport put_object(): Wrap ray.get_runtime_context().current_actor in try/except RuntimeError so the driver context (which raises) cleanly sets src_actor=None. Validate that driver-side puts require a one-sided transport - two-sided transports (NCCL, GLOO) need an actor context to coordinate the send. free_object_primary_copy(): When src_actor is None the primary copy lives in the driver's own RDT store, not on a remote actor. Call __ray_free__ directly in-process instead of dispatching .remote() on a None handle (which would crash). trigger_out_of_band_tensor_transfer(): Guard the "sent back to src" warning and the src==dst intra-process skip with `src_actor is not None` to avoid AttributeError when the object was created by the driver rather than an actor. An implementation option can be found here: [https://github.com/ray-project/ray/commit/088dc52412261ab9d95e9222d7dff89bc66f3551](url) ### Use case Non ray actors can be the source of memory from where a ray actor would want to be reading with one sided transport. current implementation requires a copy to a ray actor in the source side before calling ray.put . enabling a non ray actor to call put and free with one sided transport will eliminate the copy

signals.title: [Core][Data][CoreWorker]Discussion: remaining gRPC thread amplification with many task workers per node
signals.text: ### Description ## What happened + What you expected to happen We are investigating unexpectedly high native thread counts in Ray Data task workers on Ray **2.55.1**. Ray has already made several improvements related to worker thread counts: - #54988 / #36936 added `RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads`, allowing Raylet to pass a gRPC internal CPU-count hint to worker processes. - #58771 / #58351 introduced `RAY_core_worker_num_server_call_thread` and reduced the default CoreWorker gRPC reply executor to 2 threads. - #63685 later added cgroup-aware CPU sizing for several RayConfig-based thread pools. These changes are helpful. However, in our workload, a high worker-density node can still accumulate a large number of process-local gRPC-related threads. This issue is not requesting that CoreWorkers share a single RPC endpoint. We understand that each CoreWorker needs an independent endpoint for worker-to-worker direct calls, actor/task RPC, and process-level failure isolation. Our concern is the node-level multiplication effect: ```text number of worker processes × per-worker gRPC/runtime thread count ``` When a high-core node runs many one-CPU worker processes, each process brings its own gRPC runtime and associated native threads. Even after applying the existing worker gRPC CPU hint, the aggregate Pod-level thread count remains high. ## Environment - Ray version: `2.55.1` - Workload: Ray Data task workers - One worker Pod - Pod resources: `50 CPU / 500 GB memory` - Normal Ray task workers: `num_cpus=1` - Concurrent task workers: approximately `49` - Workload concurrency, input size, and Pod resource configuration were held constant across experiments. ## Measurements We sampled representative worker processes and grouped native threads by Linux thread name. | Configuration | `event_engine` threads | `nexting_thread` threads | Total threads per representative worker | Peak Pod thread count | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Default | 32 | 16 | ~341 | ~7200 | | `RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads=4` | 20 | 2 | ~115 | ~5800 | The setting reduced peak Pod thread count by approximately **19%**. We did not observe an obvious throughput or latency regression in this workload. The thread-name counts above were collected from the operating system. We would appreciate confirmation of the exact gRPC / Ray components corresponding to the observed names, especially `event_engine` and `nexting_thread`. For example, the thread names were collected with commands similar to: ```bash ps -L -p <pid> -o tid,comm ``` or: ```bash for task in /proc/<pid>/task/*; do cat "$task/comm" done | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr ``` ## Relevant configuration path Our understanding of the current worker-side configuration path is: ```text RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads ↓ Raylet worker startup ↓ RAY_num_grpc_internal_threads in the spawned worker environment ↓ Ray-patched gRPC CPU-count detection ↓ gRPC internal runtime / EventEngine sizing ``` We also understand that the CoreWorker server-call reply executor is separately controlled by: ```text RAY_core_worker_num_server_call_thread ``` and defaults to a small value in current Ray versions. This appears to be an important improvement, but it seems to cover the CoreWorker server-call reply executor rather than all possible gRPC EventEngine/runtime thread sources. ## Why this matters For a high-core node with many one-CPU worker processes, the per-process overhead can still become significant at node level. For illustration, consider a hypothetical 192-CPU node running approximately 192 worker processes. Using the observed thread-name counts above: ```text Default: 192 × (32 event_engine + 16 nexting_thread) ≈ 9216 threads ``` With the reduced gRPC CPU hint: ```text RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads=4: 192 × (20 event_engine + 2 nexting_thread) ≈ 4224 threads ``` These are not exact predictions for every workload or deployment, but they show the multiplication effect. Even mostly idle native threads consume operational budget through: - PID / cgroup `pids.max` usage; - native thread stack reservation and memory overhead; - scheduler overhead; - thread startup and teardown overhead; - increased risk of `pthread_create` / `EAGAIN` failures. This is especially concerning because related reports have already observed worker startup or thread creation failures on high-core systems: - #48700 - #54225 - #59626 ## What we tried We set the following before starting Ray workers: ```bash export RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads=4 ``` This materially reduced worker and Pod thread count without an obvious workload-level performance regression. However, this setting changes a gRPC CPU-count hint rather than expressing a direct worker thread budget. It is therefore difficult for us to know: - whether it is intended as a supported production tuning interface; - which exact gRPC components it changes; - whether it limits initial thread creation only or also runtime growth; - and what values are expected to be safe for different workload types. ## Discussion We would appreciate feedback from Ray maintainers and the community on how this behavior is intended to work and how it should be approached. We understand that each CoreWorker needs an independent RPC endpoint and process-level isolation. We are not assuming that worker processes should necessarily share a single RPC endpoint or that there is one simple solution for all workloads. Our main concern is the node-level multiplication effect: when a high-core node runs many one-CPU worker processes, each process brings its own gRPC runtime and related threads. Even after applying the existing worker gRPC CPU hint, the aggregate thread count can remain large. We would like to better understand the current design, expected operating envelope, and the tradeoffs involved. Questions we would especially appreciate help with: 1. Is `RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads` intended to be a supported production tuning knob for worker processes, or should it be considered an internal escape hatch? 2. Can maintainers clarify which thread pools or gRPC subsystems are affected by: - `RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads` - `RAY_core_worker_num_server_call_thread` - `RAY_num_server_call_thread` 3. In particular, does `RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads`: - affect EventEngine initial thread creation; - constrain EventEngine growth; - affect every EventEngine instance in a CoreWorker process; - or affect only some gRPC subsystems? 4. Is there an existing supported way to set a direct per-CoreWorker limit for EventEngine or other gRPC runtime threads, rather than indirectly changing the gRPC CPU-count hint? 5. For high worker-density nodes, are there existing capacity guidelines or tested configurations covering: - one or approximately one worker per CPU; - high-core hosts; - many Ray Data task workers in a single Pod; - expected worker and Pod thread counts; - `pids.max`, `ulimit -u`, and native-thread stack considerations? 6. Does the cgroup-aware CPU sizing work from #63685 also apply to the CPU count seen by the patched gRPC runtime in workers? If not, is that an area where the current behavior could be improved? Potential areas for discussion might include: - clearer documentation and observability for the existing worker-side thread controls; - a direct per-worker gRPC / EventEngine thread limit; - more conservative defaults for CPU-count-driven gRPC internals in task workers; - a per-node budget or admission mechanism for worker-side RPC threads; - automatic sizing that considers cgroup limits and worker density; - or, where compatible with process isolation and fault-tolerance requirements, consolidation or sharing of selected transport/event-loop resources. We are not proposing a specific architecture here. We would like to understand which directions are technically realistic and aligned with Ray's design goals. ## Willingness to contribute We are happy to help investigate and validate this. If there is a preferred benchmark, diagnostic format, or specific hypothesis the community would like tested, we would be happy to run it and report the results. ## Additional measurements we can provide We can provide the same workload and thread-name breakdown for a matrix such as: ```text default RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads=1 RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads=2 RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads=4 RAY_core_worker_num_server_call_thread=1 RAY_core_worker_num_server_call_thread=2 RAY_worker_num_grpc_internal_threads=4 RAY_core_worker_num_server_call_thread=1 ``` We can also compare the results across Ray versions, including a version that contains #63685. ## Related issues and PRs Issues: - #36936 — Too many threads in Ray worker - #48700 — Ray crashes when too many cores are visible - #54225 — Thread creation error, even with environment variables all set to 1 - #55215 — Make third party library thread count static in worker - #58351 — Same actor/task has different number of threads in different environments - #59626 — Resource exhaustion / `pthread_create` failures in a Ray workload - #63476 — Default GCS thread number considers cgroup Pull requests: - #54988 — Configurable worker gRPC internal thread count - #58771 — Limit CoreWorker gRPC reply threads to 2 by default - #63685 — Consider cgroup limit when fetching CPU ### Use case _No response_

signals.title: [Core][KubeRay] Autoscaler sends all log records, including INFO, to stderr
signals.text: ## What happened + What you expected to happen `_setup_logging()` in `python/ray/autoscaler/_private/kuberay/run_autoscaler.py` attaches a single `logging._StderrHandler` to the root logger, so **every** autoscaler log record — INFO included — is written to the container's **stderr**. The function's own docstring says it should be stdout: ```python def _setup_logging(log_dir: str) -> None: """Log to autoscaler log file (typically, /tmp/ray/session_latest/logs/monitor.*) Also log to pod stdout (logs viewable with `kubectl logs <head-pod> -c autoscaler`). ``` but the implementation writes stderr, and nothing writes to stdout at all: ```python level = logging.getLevelName(ray_constants.LOGGER_LEVEL.upper()) # default "info" stderr_handler = logging._StderrHandler() stderr_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter(ray_constants.LOGGER_FORMAT)) stderr_handler.setLevel(level) logging.root.setLevel(level) logging.root.addHandler(stderr_handler) # The stdout handler was set up in the Ray CLI entry point. # See ray.scripts.scripts::cli(). ``` **That trailing comment is stale.** `ray.scripts.scripts::cli()` calls `ray._private.ray_logging.setup_logger()`, which only re-sets the level and re-formats handlers already present on the `ray` logger — it never calls `addHandler`. And `setup_component_logger()`, called a few lines earlier in this same function, calls `ray._private.log.clear_logger("ray")`, which *empties* the `ray` logger's handlers. The reproduction script below prints the resulting handler list; no handler targets stdout. ### Why this matters Kubernetes' CRI log format records the stream each line arrived on, per line: ``` TIMESTAMP STREAM TAG CONTENT 2016-10-06T00:17:09.669794202Z stdout P log content 1 ``` (<https://github.com/kubernetes/design-proposals-archive/blob/main/node/kubelet-cri-logging.md>) Log collectors commonly derive a line's severity from that `STREAM` field rather than parsing the `INFO` token out of the message body, so on a KubeRay cluster with log collection routine autoscaler output is ingested as errors. The measurement below is consistent with that. Measured on a production KubeRay cluster (Datadog), autoscaler sidecar, **idle** cluster, 20 minutes: | | count | |---|---| | `status:error` | 2392 | | `status:info` | 0 | | `status:warn` | 0 | Over 24h the same container logged 63,048 `skipping idle termination` lines and zero scale events, drains, patches or exceptions. Every one of those lines was classified as an error, so the container's error rate carries no signal and cannot be alerted on. ### Expected Sub-WARNING records on stdout, WARNING and above on stderr — the conventional split — so severity survives log collection. `monitor.log` should keep receiving every level, since it backs the dashboard and the State API (`/api/v0/logs`). ### Origin This looks like an unintended regression from #34182 ("Global logging format changes"). Before that PR the code read: ```python logger_name="ray", # Root of the logging hierarchy for Ray code. ) # Logs will also be written to the container's stdout. # The stdout handler was set up in the Ray CLI entry point. ``` #34182 removed the `# Logs will also be written to the container's stdout.` line, added the `_StderrHandler`, and left the `# The stdout handler was set up in the Ray CLI entry point.` line dangling. The intent recorded in the original comment (and still in the docstring) was stdout. Note that #33652, which introduced `logging._StderrHandler` for Rich `FileProxy` compatibility, touched only `python/ray/_private/ray_logging.py` — it never touched `run_autoscaler.py`, and it was not a severity-routing decision. Same bug class as #32339 ("[Serve][Dashboard] Ray Serve actor logs show up in .err files instead of .out files"), which was accepted as `bug`/`P2`/`observability`. Adjacent to #48651. ## Versions / Dependencies - Ray: reproduced on `master` (`9c6ffee9a5`) and on the `3.0.0.dev0` nightly (`eb5882b7ba`). Present since #34182 (Ray 2.4). - Python: 3.12 - OS: reproduced on macOS locally; observed in production on Linux / KubeRay. ## Reproduction script No cluster required — this calls the logging setup directly and reports which stream each level lands on. ```python import io, logging, os, sys, tempfile from ray.autoscaler._private.kuberay.run_autoscaler import _setup_logging logging.root.handlers.clear() tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp() out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO() real_out, real_err = sys.stdout, sys.stderr sys.stdout, sys.stderr = out, err try: _setup_logging(tmp) log = logging.getLogger("ray.autoscaler._private.kuberay.run_autoscaler") log.info("INFO-MARKER skipping idle termination") log.warning("WARN-MARKER") for h in logging.root.handlers: h.flush() finally: sys.stdout, sys.stderr = real_out, real_err print("root handlers:", [type(h).__name__ for h in logging.root.handlers]) print("stdout bytes:", len(out.getvalue())) print("INFO on stdout?", "INFO-MARKER" in out.getvalue()) print("INFO on stderr?", "INFO-MARKER" in err.getvalue()) print("INFO in monitor.log?", "INFO-MARKER" in open(os.path.join(tmp, "monitor.log")).read()) ``` Actual output: ``` root handlers: ['RotatingFileHandler', '_StderrHandler'] stdout bytes: 0 INFO on stdout? False INFO on stderr? True INFO in monitor.log? True ``` Expected: `INFO on stdout? True`, `INFO on stderr? False`, `monitor.log` unchanged. ### Why `RAY_LOGGER_LEVEL=warning` is not a workaround Raising the level silences `monitor.log` too. `setup_component_logger()` is gated on the same `ray_constants.LOGGER_LEVEL`, and `logging.root.setLevel(level)` runs after it, so INFO calls short-circuit in `Logger.isEnabledFor` and never reach the rotating file handler. That removes the dashboard/State API copy of the logs, which is the copy you actually want to keep. (Raised in ray-project/kuberay#4095, documented in ray-project/kuberay#4104.) ## Issue Severity Medium: It is a significant difficulty but I can work around it.
signals.author: vivekmahajan

signals.title: [Data] Fused map functions are serialized with every shuffle-map task
signals.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen When Ray Data fuses a `MapOperator` into `RandomShuffle` or shuffle-based `Repartition`, the fused upstream map function is stored directly in `ShuffleTaskSpec.map_args`. Pull- and push-based schedulers expand those args into every shuffle-map task submission. A UDF that captures large immutable state is therefore serialized once per shuffle-map task. Currently, a 100 MiB captured closure with 10 input blocks reached about 1004 MiB incremental peak object-store usage in a local pull-shuffle benchmark. The fix reduced the same case to about 104 MiB. The growth is approximately closure size multiplied by map-task count. It should serialize the fused map function once, store it in Ray's object store, and pass its `ObjectRef` as a top-level positional argument to each shuffle-map task. Ray Core should resolve the function before invoking the task. ### Versions / Dependencies on `master` ### Reproduction script ```python import numpy as np import ray state = np.ones(100 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=np.uint8) def udf(batch): assert state[0] == 1 return batch ray.init(num_cpus=4) ( ray.data.range(500_000, override_num_blocks=10) .map_batches(udf, batch_size=None, batch_format="numpy") .random_shuffle(seed=0) .materialize() ) ``` ### Issue Severity Medium: It is a significant difficulty but I can work around it.
signals.author: viiccwen

signals.title: [Data] Support refreshing vended-credentials for native catalog Iceberg path
signals.text: ### Description Databricks UC vends short-lived storage credentials with 1h TTL. This means any long-running Ray Data job will fail to write to Iceberg tables after that. 2 approaches I can think of - **Workaround (bypass vending)**: sending `header.X-Iceberg-Access-Delegation: ""` [defaults to `vended-credentials`](https://py.iceberg.apache.org/configuration/) and injecting the cloud's storage config so the backend falls through to the job identity's own refreshable credential chain. The native catalog cannot express this as it hardcodes the header https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/227da64f41c387e82a01293f062d68382cc89c16/python/ray/data/catalog.py#L286 - **Correct fix**: vended credentials are short-lived *by design* (least-privilege), so any path that resolves once on the driver and pickles `catalog_kwargs` into write tasks will hit a TTL on a long run. Moving `catalog.resolve()` into each read/write task should fix this. ### Use case A long-running batch-inference job that writes the output to an Iceberg table. This would require a single `write_iceberg` that has a data-file phase lasts more than 1h.
signals.author: nkvuong

signals.title: [RLlib] `Checkpointable.from_checkpoint` should have return type `typing.Self` instead of `Checkpointable`
signals.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen When loading e.g. a `EnvToModulePipeline` from a checkpoint via `EnvToModulePipeline.from_checkpoint(...)` the returned type is `Checkpointable` which requires manual casting to `EnvToModulePipeline` to ensure type checkers correctly understand the loaded checkpoint. `typing.Self` allows base classes to implement functions that return itself in a way which respects subclasses. ```python from typing import Self, reveal_type class A: def f(self) -> Self: return self class B(A): pass a = A() b = B() reveal_type(a.f()) # Revealed type "A" reveal_type(b.f()) # Revealed type "B" ``` If the return type of `EnvToModulePipeline.from_checkpoint` would be annotated as `typing.Self` then a checkpoint would return an instance of the right class in a way that type checkers can understand. ### Versions / Dependencies Ray 2.53.0 (but the same can be observed with 2.57.0) Python 3.11 OS Linux ### Reproduction script ```python import os from ray.rllib.core.rl_module import RLModule module = RLModule() module.save_to_path(f"file://{os.getcwd()}/test") ckpt_module = RLModule.from_checkpoint("file:///albus/test") ``` Type checkers now show the type of `ckpt_module` to be `Checkpointable` and not `RLModule`, as one would expect. Runtime type is correctly `RLModule`. ### Issue Severity Low: It annoys or frustrates me.
signals.author: cyianor

signals.title: [Data] Make BigQuery (GCP) client construction injectable in read_bigquery / write_bigquery
signals.text: ### Description `ray.data.read_bigquery` and `Dataset.write_bigquery` construct their Google Cloud clients through hardcoded private module-level factories in `python/ray/data/_internal/datasource/bigquery_datasource.py`: ```python def _create_client(project_id: str): from google.cloud import bigquery return bigquery.Client(project=project_id, client_info=_create_client_info()) def _create_read_client(): from google.cloud import bigquery_storage return bigquery_storage.BigQueryReadClient(client_info=_create_client_info_gapic()) ``` Every call site — `BigQueryDatasource.get_read_tasks`, `BigQueryDatasource._validate_dataset_table_exist`, `BigQueryDatasink.on_write_start`, and the per-block write task (which reaches across modules into `bigquery_datasource._create_client`) — calls these directly. There is no seam for the caller to influence client construction. Concretely, this means a user of `read_bigquery` / `write_bigquery` cannot: - **Pass explicit credentials.** Only Application Default Credentials work. Impersonated service accounts, a `google.oauth2.service_account.Credentials` loaded from a secret manager, or per-dataset credentials in a multi-tenant job are all impossible without mutating process-global ADC state (`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`), which is process-wide and racy when several datasets in one job target different projects. - **Set `client_options`.** No way to point at a regional endpoint (`api_endpoint`), use a Private Service Connect endpoint, or set `quota_project_id`. - **Tune the client.** Custom `google.api_core.retry.Retry` policies, timeouts, or a custom transport / `requests.Session` are unreachable. - **Configure the Storage Read API client at all.** `_create_read_client()` accepts no arguments whatsoever — only `client_info` is set. Credentials, `client_options`, and transport are all unreachable for the data-plane client, even though it is the client that does the actual bulk read inside every read task. - **Test without monkeypatching.** `python/ray/data/tests/datasource/test_bigquery.py` has to `monkeypatch.setattr(bigquery, "Client", client_mock)` — it patches the vendor library's global namespace because there is no injection point. That is fragile and leaks across the module boundary between the datasink and the datasource. Ray Data already has a precedent for exactly this shape of extensibility: `DatabricksCredentialProvider` in `python/ray/data/_internal/datasource/databricks_credentials.py`, an ABC with concrete implementations, injected via a `credential_provider` argument on `read_databricks_tables`. The BigQuery path has no equivalent. ### Use case I run Ray Data jobs that read from and write to BigQuery projects the job process is not natively authenticated against — credentials are fetched at runtime and differ per dataset within a single job. Today the only way to do this is to mutate `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` before each read, which does not work when two reads against different projects are in flight concurrently, and does not survive being shipped to a worker at all. More broadly, anyone who needs a regional endpoint, a quota project, an impersonated service account, or custom retry behaviour on the BigQuery client currently has to fork the datasource. ### Proposed direction Introduce a `BigQueryClientProvider` abstraction, mirroring the existing `DatabricksCredentialProvider` pattern: - An ABC exposing `get_client()` (`bigquery.Client`, control plane) and `get_read_client()` (`bigquery_storage.BigQueryReadClient`, data plane). - A default implementation preserving today's behaviour, extended to accept `credentials`, `client_options`, and extra client kwargs, and to correctly pass `project_id` through to the read client. - An optional `client_provider` argument on `read_bigquery` and `write_bigquery`; omitting it keeps the current behaviour exactly. One design constraint worth stating explicitly, because it rules out the obvious alternative of accepting a live client object: **the provider must be the injected unit, not the client.** `BigQueryDatasource` and `BigQueryDatasink` are pickled and shipped to workers, and Google's clients are not serializable — this is the root cause of #45197 (`cannot pickle 'google._upb._message.Descriptor' object`). A provider that constructs clients lazily on the worker and drops any cached client from its pickled state is serializable; a bare `bigquery.Client` is not. The provider ABC also gives users a documented place to build a fully customized client themselves. This would additionally let `test_bigquery.py` inject a fake provider instead of monkeypatching `google.cloud.bigquery.Client` globally. I have a working implementation of this and am happy to open a PR if maintainers agree with the direction. <!-- AI assistance was used in researching and drafting this issue. -->
signals.author: onratlgn

signals.title: [Data] MCAPDatasource: support file-level packed output to enable shuffle-free episode aggregation
signals.text: ### Description Add an option to `ray.data.read_mcap` (and to `MCAPDatasource` directly) to optionally return **one row per MCAP file**, with all messages of that file packed into position-aligned list columns (e.g. `datas`, `topics`, `log_times`) plus a scalar `path` column identifying the source file. This lets users who treat a file as the atomic unit (per-recording "episode" aggregation) do the work in a downstream `map`/`map_batches` on a single row, instead of being forced to run a global `groupby("path").map_groups(...)` and pay its shuffle cost. The existing message-level path, schema, and predicate pushdown (`topics` / `time_range` / `message_types`) should remain the default and be unaffected. ### Use case We work with embodied AI / robotics data where the **MCAP file is the natural unit of a recording session (an "episode")**: each file contains several hundred thousand messages spread across multiple topics (cameras, IMU, audio, control commands, etc.) and is on the order of hundreds of MB to ~1.5 GB. Downstream operators (e.g. multi-stream time alignment, whole-session processing, batch ingestion keyed by recording) all need to see **every topic of the whole file together** — a single message, or a single topic, is not enough to do the work. With today's `read_mcap` we get one row per message, so the messages of one file get scattered across many blocks throughout the cluster. To re-assemble them by episode we have to do: ```python ds = ray.data.read_mcap("/data/sessions/", include_paths=True) ds = ds.groupby("path").map_groups(my_episode_fn) ``` This `groupby` is the bottleneck of our pipeline: - It introduces a **stage-wide barrier**: all read tasks must finish before any aggregation starts, killing the read → decode pipeline parallelism we'd otherwise get. - The shuffled intermediate carries per-message metadata (schema, encodings, paths) repeatedly, blowing up into **hundreds of GB of network traffic** for a few TB of source data. - End-to-end job time grows significantly compared to a theoretical "read once, decode once" path. The key observation is that the read task is **already scheduled per file** — every message of a given episode is co-located in the same read task *before* any shuffle ever happens. Packing them into one row at that point lets downstream `map`/`map_batches` consume the full episode directly, with **zero shuffle**. We'd like Ray Data to expose this as a first-class option on `read_mcap` / `MCAPDatasource`, so any user with file-as-atom workloads (MCAP, ROS bags, sensor logs, etc.) can opt into shuffle-free aggregation without writing a custom datasource. The packed output should reuse the existing column semantics and the existing predicate pushdown on `topics` / `time_range` / `message_types`, so users don't lose any filtering capability by switching granularity. We're not attached to any specific API shape — a boolean flag, an `output_granularity` option, or something else entirely would all work for us. A few questions for the maintainers: - Is file-level packed output something you'd consider in scope for `read_mcap`, or is it better handled as a more generic `FileBasedDatasource` capability (which would also benefit other file-per-recording formats like ROS bags)? - If there's an existing way to achieve shuffle-free per-file aggregation that we've missed, pointers would be appreciated. We'd be happy to contribute a PR if there's interest.
signals.author: eggiter

signals.title: [Data] MCAPDatasource: batched (streaming) message reads to reduce peak memory and enable intra-file pipelining
signals.text: ### Description `MCAPDatasource._read_stream` currently accumulates all messages of a file into a single block and yields it once at the end. Propose an optional `batch_size` parameter for `ray.data.read_mcap` / `MCAPDatasource`: when set, `_read_stream` yields one block per batch instead of one block per file. This reduces a read task's peak memory from "whole file" to "one batch", and lets downstream operators start consuming while the rest of the file is still being read. Default `None` keeps the current behavior exactly; output schema and predicate pushdown are unchanged — only block boundaries change. The exact sizing semantics (message count vs. target block size in bytes) is open for discussion. ### Use case MCAP recordings can be large. Today each read task buffers the entire file's messages before yielding anything, so peak memory scales with file size multiplied by concurrent read tasks, and downstream stages cannot overlap with the read within a file. Daft's `read_mcap` offers exactly this knob (`batch_size`, default 1000) for the same reasons. Within Ray itself, `_read_stream`'s `Iterator[Block]` protocol already supports yielding multiple blocks per file, and other file-based datasources use it that way (Parquet by row group, text formats by chunk) — MCAP is currently the exception with its single whole-file yield. (For broader context, #65640 proposes an unrelated file-level packed output; this proposal is independent of it.)
signals.author: eggiter

signals.title: [Core] ObjectRefGenerator async timeout polls leak waiter tasks
signals.text: ## Summary `ObjectRefGenerator._next_async` creates a new asyncio waiter for each timeout poll but does not cancel or await the waiter when the timeout expires. ## Reproduction When the next object in a streaming generator is not ready: 1. `_next_async` creates a task for `_suppress_exceptions(ref)`. 2. It calls `asyncio.wait(..., timeout=timeout_s)`. 3. On timeout it returns a nil `ObjectRef`. 4. The pending waiter task is discarded without cleanup. Repeated finite-timeout polls therefore accumulate pending tasks that retain the unresolved object reference. The issue is reproducible with the equivalent asyncio control flow: 100 timeout polls leave pending waiter tasks and produce pending-task warnings when the event loop closes. ## Expected behavior A timed-out poll should return the nil reference while cleaning up its local waiter task. ## Proposed direction Keep the waiter in a local variable and cancel/await it when it remains pending after the timeout. The fix should preserve the existing stream cursor and timeout behavior. I have a focused patch and regression test that verifies repeated timeout polls do not leave new pending tasks.
signals.author: hsusul

signals.title: [Data] Migrate CSV Datasource to Datasource v2
signals.text: ### Description Migrate `ray.data.read_csv()` from the legacy `FileBasedDatasource` implementation to DataSourceV2. When `DataContext.use_datasource_v2` is enabled, `read_csv()` should construct a CSV DataSourceV2 and use the `ListFiles → ReadFiles` execution path, while preserving the existing public API and behavior. The migration should: - Add the CSV-specific DataSourceV2 reader, scanner, and datasource components. - Reuse the existing DSv2 file listing and partitioning infrastructure. - Reuse or extend `LineDelimitedFileChunker` to split large, uncompressed CSV files. - Correctly handle CSV headers and records that cross chunk boundaries, without missing or duplicating rows. - Read compressed CSV files as whole files when byte-range chunking isn't supported. - Preserve schema inference across chunks and multiple input files. - Maintain compatibility with: - `read_options`, `parse_options`, `convert_options`, and other PyArrow CSV arguments. - `filesystem` and `arrow_open_stream_args`. - `partition_filter` and `partitioning`. - `include_paths`. - `ignore_missing_paths`. - `shuffle`, `file_extensions`, and `override_num_blocks`. - Local, remote, and `local://` paths. - Preserve actionable error messages for invalid CSV input. - Add unit and integration tests covering DSv1/DSv2 behavior parity. ### Use case CSV is one of Ray Data's primary file-based datasources, but it still uses the legacy datasource execution path. As a result, CSV reads don't benefit from the common DataSourceV2 architecture used for distributed file listing, read-task planning, and large-file chunking. Migrating CSV provides consistent behavior across file-based datasources and enables large CSV files to be read with better parallelism while maintaining compatibility with existing `ray.data.read_csv()` workloads.
